comment: Per-resort corrections applied by pipeline/normalize_osm.py (ADR-036). See whistler-blackcomb.overrides.json for the format. Snowshoe Basin under the village on Cheat Mountain's ridge with the Western Territory across the road (one polygon, way/1244062674, named Snowshoe Mountain in OpenStreetMap, 2.95 km2; the trail map's 'Located across the street from the Powder Monkey lift': skiers cross the road from the Powder Monkey's top to the Western Express, so the two are one ski area joined on snow). Silver Creek, 1.4 km north across a wooded valley, is joined to them by no lift or trail and has its own map (silver-creek.overrides.json) by the owner's rule of 2026-11-14, which retired the combined map snowshoe-v1: the trail map draws no run or lift between Silver Creek and the Basin and a bus stop at each base, snowshoemtn.com's Silver Creek page offers a 'free shuttle to & from' and its shuttle page runs continuous loops between Silver Creek, the Village and Top of the World (the Internet Archive's copies of 2025-03-13 and 2024-12-12; the site answers automated requests with a bot wall). Silver Creek's polygon (way/1311361876, also named Snowshoe Mountain) is a listed neighbour in resorts.json. Nothing of either is reached only by road but the Western Territory's crossing of the street, which the map marks. Every named run and lift checked on 2026-11-14 against Snowshoe's trail map (the James Niehues painting with its Western Territory inset; skiresort.info's copy, 3000 x 1013 px, which that site lists for the 2025/2026 season, the same file the combined map was checked against on 2026-11-12; snowshoemtn.com answers curl and WebFetch alike with a bot wall, so the resort's own copy could not be read), read enlarged two to five times; the OpenStreetMap data in the window are the combined map's of 2026-11-12, an answer pinned to its timestamp being the same, element for element. Its key: Easier (green circle), More Difficult (blue square), Most Difficult (one black diamond) and Extremely Difficult (two), as OSM's easy, intermediate, advanced and expert; Terrain Park (orange hatching, with S, M and L), Gladed Terrain (black hatching), Uphill Routes and Tubing Terrain (dashed lines), Terrain Based Learning and Slow Skiing Area. Its lifts here: Soaring Eagle Express, Ballhooter High Speed Quad, Grabhammer, Skidder, Powder Monkey, Powderidge and, in the Western Territory, the Western Express. The resort's lift and trail status could not be read (the bot wall), so the printed map is the source and wins. OpenStreetMap draws most runs twice, as a line and as an outline (area=yes); overrides name each way. All of OSM's named runs carry the map's rating: the glades (Sawmill Glades, Knot Bumper Glades and Sunset Glades, one diamond each) are tagged backcountry in OSM and lie inside the polygon, so they stay in bounds by the rule. Names from the map: Sunset Glades (OSM SunSet Glades). Names hidden as descriptions the map does not print: Mid-Station (the connector at the Western Express's mid-station) and To Western Territory (an outline at the Powder Monkey's top). Names that differ from the map only by a section stay as OSM has them: Cupp Run and Shay's Revenge, single ways where the map labels an upper and a lower part (CUPP RUN and LOWER CUPP RUN, both one diamond; Lower Shay's Revenge, two diamonds, is OSM's own way), and Whistlepunk (the map's UPPER WHISTLEPUNK and WHISTLEPUNK). Parks: Progression Park and Evolution Park are snow parks in OSM; Evolution Park's outline, drawn as a downhill run there, gets the park flag as its line has. Lifts: the seven chairs are in OSM under the map's names and no lift name repeats with Silver Creek's; Village Access, a 44 m carpet OSM maps at the Skidder's bottom that the painting does not draw, stays (no source says it has gone). OSM gaps (shipped as at Palisades Tahoe): Lower Ballhooter (blue), Shamrock and Black Bear (green, by the Powderidge top) are not named in OSM.

overrides.reason: SunSet Glades: the gladed line between Cupp Run and Shay's Revenge under the Western Express, which Snowshoe's trail map (the James Niehues painting with its Western Territory inset; skiresort.info's copy, 3000 x 1013 px, which that site lists for the 2025/2026 season; snowshoemtn.com answers curl and WebFetch alike with a bot wall, so the resort's own copy could not be read) labels Sunset Glades with one black diamond. Capitalisation from the map; OSM's rating is the map's.

Evolution Park's outline: Snowshoe's trail map (the James Niehues painting with its Western Territory inset; skiresort.info's copy, 3000 x 1013 px, which that site lists for the 2025/2026 season; snowshoemtn.com answers curl and WebFetch alike with a bot wall, so the resort's own copy could not be read) draws Evolution Park as terrain park (orange hatching, features M-L) beside the Powderidge chair; OSM tags its line a snow park and its outline a downhill run. Park flag from the map; OSM's rating is kept.

Mid-Station: a 202 m connector at the Western Express's mid-station between Cupp Run and Shay's Revenge, which Snowshoe's trail map (the James Niehues painting with its Western Territory inset; skiresort.info's copy, 3000 x 1013 px, which that site lists for the 2025/2026 season; snowshoemtn.com answers curl and WebFetch alike with a bot wall, so the resort's own copy could not be read) draws without a name; 'Mid-Station' names the lift's station, not a run. The name is hidden; OSM's rating stays.

To Western Territory: a 164 m outline at the Powder Monkey's top where skiers cross the road to the Western Territory, which Snowshoe's trail map (the James Niehues painting with its Western Territory inset; skiresort.info's copy, 3000 x 1013 px, which that site lists for the 2025/2026 season; snowshoemtn.com answers curl and WebFetch alike with a bot wall, so the resort's own copy could not be read) does not name ('Located across the street from the Powder Monkey lift'); the name is a direction, not a run. The name is hidden; OSM's rating stays.
